clips.title: The story
paras: Call of Water is an initiation rite that directs rising Horde shaman from the heights of Thunder Bluff toward the eastern shores of the Barrens. To commune with the cleansing element of water, an initiate must seek out the recluse Islen Waterseer. This meeting marks the first step on a spiritual journey to earn the Water Totem.

Having mastered the unyielding earth and the untamed flame, an aspiring shaman is eventually deemed ready to study the deeper mysteries of the elements. In Thunder Bluff, trainers like Xanis Flameweaver recognize when a student has shown enough discipline to approach the fluid, cleansing spirit of water. The journey requires leaving the windswept mesas of Mulgore behind and traveling east across the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens.

The path leads to Islen Waterseer, a quiet mystic who lives away from the bustling settlements, residing in a humble fishing shack on the eastern coast south of Ratchet and the mouth of the Southfury River. Standing at the edge of the great ocean, Islen reads the readiness of travelers by how the elements linger about them. Seeing the steady earth, the brisk wind, and the warmth of fire already bound to the seeker's spirit, she prepares them for the trials required to understand water's purity.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: Long has it been since you were last tested, friend. You have shown patience thus far in your studies, but the time has come for you to learn more. The time has come for you to learn about the purity of water.
Seek out Islen Waterseer in the Barrens. She is along the eastern coast, south of the Southfury River and Ratchet. You will find her there at her fishing hut. Good luck to you, friend.

clips.title: Completion
paras: The wind approaches you quickly from the horizon; the earth is steady beneath your feet; and your spirit is already warmed by fire—I would say it is time for you to learn about the purity of water.
Your path has led you this far, and your spirit will give you the strength to carry on even further. But the first step is yours to take.
